STEP 1 - Scene: A top-down photo of a white square plate holding two short cross-section pieces of corn on the cob (cooked, no visible butter or sauce).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate's longest width (diagonal) is about 26 cm in the image, but it is a square-ish side plate, so the side is roughly 21 cm. Area is about 21 × 21 ≈ 440 cm² less the rounded corners, so ~400 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: two corn cob rounds.

STEP 4 - Area: In pixels, one piece is about 100 px across and the other about 95 px. The plate is about 380 px per side, which is ~21 cm, so ~18 px/cm. That makes the pieces ~5.5 cm and ~5 cm across.
- Piece 1: π × 2.75² ≈ 23.7 cm²
- Piece 2: π × 2.6² ≈ 21 cm²
Total ≈ 45 cm², or about 11% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each piece is about 2.5 cm tall (the side walls are visible and the pieces look thick). Volume is 45 × 2.5 ≈ 112 ml. The cob core is included in the volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Corn on the cob is dense, with a bulk density of about 0.7 g/ml (kernels plus cob). 112 × 0.7 ≈ 79 g. I'll use ~80 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Corn on the cob, cooked, is about 96 kcal/100 g including the cob, which gives ~77 kcal. Kernels alone are about 86–130 kcal/100 g, so ~96 is reasonable.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two small corn rounds weighing ~80 g in total is plausible.
